subject: Calibrating dedicated GPU runway & SLOs for Orchid Analytics pilot
messages:
From: Samir Gupta <samir@orchidanalytics.com>
To: Rachel Kim <rachel.kim@redwood.ai>
Cc: procurement@orchidanalytics.com
Date: 2026-07-01T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Dedicated capacity sizing for pilot - quick profile

Hi Rachel,

Thanks for the demo last week — the team at Orchid is excited to move to a short pilot (6 weeks) for our customer-facing summarization flow. Before we lock the pilot, procurement needs a sketch of the dedicated GPU runway and a latency SLO fit so they can sign off.

Quick profile:
- Model: open-llm-34B (we plan to use a 4-bit quantized variant)
- Expected peak concurrency: 120 concurrent users (chat-style requests), peak burst of ~600 qps (inference requests) for ~30s during batch report times
- Average tokens per request: 350 input + 150 output = 500 tokens
- Traffic shape: 70% low-latency interactive (SLO 350ms p95), 30% async batch (SLO 2s p95)
- Estimated daily tokens: ~18M tokens/day during pilot

Can your team provide a tokens/sec / GPU estimate and a suggested safety headroom recommendation? Procurement also asked for a one-page SLA sketch.

Thanks — Samir
Samir Gupta
Head of Product
Orchid Analytics

From: Rachel Kim <rachel.kim@redwood.ai>
To: Samir Gupta <samir@orchidanalytics.com>
Cc: ben.carter@redwood.ai, priyom.das@redwood.ai, procurement@orchidanalytics.com
Date: 2026-07-01T11:04:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Dedicated capacity sizing for pilot - quick profile

Samir —

Appreciate the profile, that’s very helpful. We’ll put together a short sizing note and SLA sketch by Tuesday. A couple clarifying Qs to make the runway math tight:

1) Peak request concurrency: is 120 concurrent users mapped to 120 active sessions or to 120 simultaneous model calls? (i.e., do users batch multiple requests client-side?)
2) Can you share a small telemetry sample (timestamps, tokens in/out, response latencies) — even a CSV is fine.
3) Do you expect the 600 qps bursts to be single-region (US-only) or split globally?

I’ve looped in Ben (SE) and Priyom (inference architect) to run the tokens/sec per-GPU estimation and propose headroom. I’ll share the SLA draft and an ops runbook for the pilot.

Next steps:
- Ben/Priyom: will produce a short calc + recommended GPU slab and fallback model variants.
- Rachel -> Samir: SLA + pilot runbook + launch checklist by 2026-07-06 EOD PT.

Thanks,
Rachel Kim
Senior Account Executive, Redwood Inference

From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
To: Rachel Kim <rachel.kim@redwood.ai>, Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.ai>
Cc: Samir Gupta <samir@orchidanalytics.com>, procurement@orchidanalytics.com
Date: 2026-07-02T10:22:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Dedicated capacity sizing for pilot - quick profile

Folks — ran preliminary back-of-envelope based on Rachel/Samir notes and our measured perf for open-llm-34B 4-bit on A100-ish hardware (profiled with our runtime optimizations). Summary below; attaching a spreadsheet with the step-by-step math.

Short answer (pilot guidance):
- Median tokens/sec per GPU (4-bit, batch-adaptive runtime): ~1,100 tokens/s (single-stream interactive with small batching)
- For interactive SLO (p95 <= 350ms) we estimate ~90 concurrent interactive streams per GPU before p95 risk rises — that maps to ~50–60 qps of 500-token requests for target latency
- For efficient throughput (async batch workflows), a GPU can sustain ~6,500 tokens/s with large batching (2–3s queuing tolerated)

Orchid numbers, converted:
- Peak burst 600 qps * 500 tokens = 300,000 tokens/sec burst
- If we target keeping p95 <= 350ms for interactive portion (70% of traffic): interactive tokens/sec = 0.7 * 300k = 210k tokens/sec
- With 1,100 tokens/sec per GPU for interactive-latency-critical workloads => ~191 GPUs to meet instant p95 without further headroom

We recommend a mixed slab approach so Orchid isn’t overprovisioned for brief bursts:
1) Base slab (commit): 40 GPUs reserved to cover steady-state and predictable peaks (covers ~44k tokens/sec interactive capacity)
2) Burst pool (on-demand dedicated or hot spare): ability to spin up additional 160 GPUs in <5 min to cover sustained high bursts (covers remaining ~166k tokens/sec)
3) Routing policy: prioritize async batch to batchable GPUs and preserve interactive capacity on low-latency slab; automatic fallback to smaller quantized model (open-llm-13B) at extreme load to maintain p95 latency.

Headroom framing: for safe ops during pilot we suggest targeting 25% headroom above modeled peak for the reserved slab (i.e., treat 40 GPUs as capacity for 35 GPUs-worth of modeled load, 25% buffer) and ensure burst policy can add capacity quickly.

Notes / assumptions:
- Our tokens/sec numbers are sensitive to: sequence length variance, average tokens/request, and tail-latency amplification from concurrent KV cache pressure; I included conservative multipliers in the attached sheet.
- If Orchid can accept slightly looser p95 (e.g., 500ms) we cut the interactive GPU need by ~30% via more aggressive micro-batching.

Attachments: runway-calculation-ORCH-042.xlsx (breakdown), SLA-draft-Orchid-2026.pdf (one-page sketch).

Happy to walk through numbers — I can join your call with Samir on Wednesday.

— Ben
Ben Carter
Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference

From: Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.ai>
To: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>, Rachel Kim <rachel.kim@redwood.ai>, Samir Gupta <samir@orchidanalytics.com>
Date: 2026-07-03T09:45:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Dedicated capacity sizing for pilot - quick profile

Adding a few operational and model-fit suggestions from the inference architecture side:

- Fallback model: plan an A/B fallback to open-llm-13B quantized at ~2-bit for extreme bursts — this preserves experience while cutting tokens/sec pressure by ~2.8x.
- KV cache warmup: for chat-style sessions we recommend sticky routing (session pinned to a GPU) for the first ~20 turns, then move to stateless routing for long-tail to reduce KV pressure spikes.
- Autoscale window: 5-minute scale-up with optimistic pre-warming; scale-down at 20 minutes. Keeps cost down while giving headroom for short bursts.
- Observability: surface token-rate per model, per-route p95 latency, and queued-request depth to a pilot dashboard. We'll add a runbook alert at 70% slab utilization and urgent ops paging at 90%.

Operationally, the mixed slab approach Ben outlined is the right balance. My conservative estimate: commit 45 GPUs (we size slightly above Ben for non-modeled overhead), with rapid burst to ~200 GPUs if needed. Reserve the ability to fall back to smaller models and to route batchable flows to different priority pools.

— Priyom
Priyom Das
Principal Inference Architect, Redwood Inference

From: Rachel Kim <rachel.kim@redwood.ai>
To: Samir Gupta <samir@orchidanalytics.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>, Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.ai>, procurement@orchidanalytics.com
Date: 2026-07-06T14:08:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Dedicated capacity sizing for pilot - quick profile

Samir —

Attached is a concise summary for procurement and your engineering team:
- Sizing recommendation: start pilot with a 45-GPU reserved slab (A100-class), plus ability to burst up to 200 GPUs within ~5 minutes via our burst pool.
- Expected SLO fit: p95 <= 350ms for interactive flows under modeled steady-state and moderate bursts; for sustained massive bursts we'll activate fallback to 13B quantized to preserve p95.
- Tokens/sec math: see attached runway-calculation-ORCH-042.xlsx (high-level: peak 300k tokens/sec; interactive portion ~210k tokens/sec; mix + headroom -> 45 GPU commit + burst).
- Operational controls: sticky routing for chat warmups, 5-min scale-up window, observability dashboards and alerts at 70%/90% slab utilization.

Next steps:
1) Procurement: review SLA-draft-Orchid-2026.pdf and share comments by 2026-07-09.
2) Engineering: please upload a short telemetry CSV (timestamps + tokens + sample latencies) to the Drive link so we can refine numbers before pilot start.
3) Schedule: tentative pilot kickoff 2026-07-20 — we’ll confirm capacity prep by 2026-07-15.

Let me know if you want a quick walk-through with Ben/Priyom.

Best,
Rachel Kim
Senior Account Executive, Redwood Inference
